en.headline: Tang says 999 upgrades will add real-time video and AI prioritisation by 2028
en.dek: Callers could use WhatsApp or WeChat to send live images of incidents, with information shared instantly to the Fire Services Department.
body: Secretary for Security Tang Ping-keung outlined further details of planned upgrades to the 999 emergency service, including real-time video capability and artificial intelligence to prioritise calls.

Speaking on a radio programme on Saturday, Tang said the service, announced in the Policy Address, would allow callers reporting fires or robberies to use their cameras to show the scene, enabling more accurate resource deployment. The government hopes to implement the features through apps already used by the public, such as WhatsApp and WeChat.

Information from calls would also be transmitted instantly to the Fire Services Department so its control centre can speak with the caller and view video at the same time. AI would sort different types of reports, giving priority to fires, for example, to manage high call volumes.

Tang estimated the new functions would be ready in 2028. He also noted that the police's Sharp Eye CCTV programme has helped solve more than 2,000 crimes and that mall cameras would soon be connected to the system, all in compliance with privacy laws.

zh.headline: 鄧炳強：999將增實時視像及人工智能分流 目標2028年啟用
zh.dek: 市民日後可用WhatsApp或微信拍攝現場，報案資訊即時傳送消防處，火警等優先處理。
body: 保安局局長鄧炳強進一步介紹999緊急求助服務的升級計劃，包括加入實時視像功能及以人工智能為報案排序。
鄧炳強周六在電台節目中說，《施政報告》提出的新功能，讓報火警或劫案的市民可用鏡頭拍攝現場，方便同事更精準調派資源。當局希望透過市民常用的通訊軟件如WhatsApp及微信落實。
報案資訊日後會即時傳送至消防處，消防控制中心可同時與報案人交談及觀看視頻。人工智能會將不同類型報案排序，例如優先處理火警，以分流來電。
鄧炳強估計新功能可於2028年啟用。他又提到警方「銳眼」閉路電視計劃已協助偵破逾2000宗罪案，很快會將商場鏡頭接入系統，一切合乎私隱條例。
